items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER: So the Elvin Jones Jazz Machine has been stem rolling for several decades. ... At that time you had Andrew White, Ari Brown, Ryo? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Ryo Kawasaki? No. It was Marvin Horn, I think he was playing guitar.

ctx.x: It’s the same thing that happens with Duke Ellington’s bands. I’ve seen Ben Webster walk out and six months later he comes back in and stands up and plays his solo. (Laughs) Duke thought that was perfectly alright, it’s better than not coming. That’s what it’s all about; you have to be generous in that sense. It’s trust. I trust the guys that work with me and they know it.

So the Elvin Jones Jazz Machine has been stem rolling for several decades. Ken Kimery and I first saw that group in 1980 in Mannheim, Germany. At that time you had Andrew White, Ari Brown, Ryo? Was he playing guitar?
Ryo Kawasaki? No. It was Marvin Horn, I think he was playing guitar.
